direction.premise: A modular spacecraft is both the shared construction surface and the crew’s fighting vehicle.
direction.composition: The central ship grid is surrounded by explicit workshop and crew panels; on phones those panels slide over a full-width flight field.
direction.shapeLanguage: Square hull cells and source illustrated engine, turret and reactor modules expose the playable ship architecture.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Original raster module illustrations sit on a translucent engineering grid against a restrained starfield.
direction.paletteLogic: Cyan outlines construction cells and friendly ship systems; orange signals combat, damage and pickups.
direction.typography: Locally bundled Audiowide headings and Sora control labels preserve the original technical lettering offline.
direction.signature: A crew member sits in the engine while another takes the turret; both actions affect the same ship and enemy wave.
direction.distinction: FOG uses geographic orders and ZAMAZKA uses painted restoration fragments; this port retains its source game object and the specific input loop described here.

architecture.primaryVerb: Buy and place ship modules, take a crew station, steer the shared vessel and repair systems while fighting successive waves.
architecture.physicalFeedback: A module snaps to hull cells during construction; occupied stations show their pilot and produce immediate shared movement or weapon fire.
architecture.spatialRationale: The central ship grid is surrounded by explicit workshop and crew panels; on phones those panels slide over a full-width flight field. This keeps the current game object and its real inputs spatially connected on a phone.

production.renderer: Canvas draws the original modular ship and combat sprites; stable DOM panels expose crew occupancy, inventory and repair commands.
production.focalAsset: The recovered ship module sprites and hull grid remain the main authored object; an app-specific ship-on-grid SVG supplies install identity.

motion.character: A module snaps to hull cells during construction; occupied stations show their pilot and produce immediate shared movement or weapon fire.
motion.action: Buy and place ship modules, take a crew station, steer the shared vessel and repair systems while fighting successive waves.
motion.anticipation: The current selection, room state and available control labels expose the pending operation before the player activates it.
motion.response: The next visible state responds to the actual control: A crew member sits in the engine while another takes the turret; both actions affect the same ship and enemy wave.
motion.followThrough: The resulting world, board or round state remains visible until a later explicit action changes it; no decorative transition hides the outcome.
motion.interruption: Repeated input uses the current state; pointer cancellation releases held controls and hidden tabs stop transmitting held actions.
motion.reducedMotion: The complete play state remains legible without decorative entry animations; spatial gameplay and authoritative outcomes retain their original timing.

evidence.expectedChange: The saved offline practice ship opens in its construction or combat phase using the same server rules.
